newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine rights group to try mediate Peru crisis.
newsitem.headline: Argentine rights group to try mediate Peru crisis.

text.p: The Argentine human rights group Mothers of Plaza de Mayo said on Thursday it would travel to Peru on Friday at the request of rebels to seek a negotiated settlement to the hostage crisis.

Mothers president Hebe de Bonafini told reporters the group has requested a meeting with Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori but had no official word on whether the administration accepted the rebel request for her to mediate.

Argentina's most famous human rights group said on Wednesday it was asked by the Marxist Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels to act as a go-between in talks with the government. The guerrillas are holding 72 hostages in the Japanese ambassador's home in Lima, which they stormed on Dec. 17, demanding the release of 400 jailed comrades.
"If Fujimori wants peace he can't refuse to meet with us as have leaders around the world," Bonafini said, noting her group has been in contact for many years with relatives of Peruvian prisoners.

"We are willing to do anything. If my life helps save that of others, then I will give it immediately," she told reporters. "We will talk with the Church, with the Red Cross International ... We want to go into the (ambassador's residence) and the jails to see the prisoners, trying to remain as independent as possible."

The white-scarved Mothers of the Plaza de Mayo was formed at the height of the Argentine military's "Dirty War" against leftist guerrillas in the 1970s by mothers whose children disappeared in the conflict.
Bonafini was confident the crisis would end peacefully. "If the two sides were really so inflexible, the residence would already have blown up," she said.
"Improving the sub-human living conditions of prisoners could be a starting point for negotiations," she added.
Talks to end the crisis at a Red Cross safe house between the MRTA and government appear to have stalled, with Fujimori refusing to free jailed MRTA members.
Representatives of the Vatican, the Red Cross and the Canadian government are serving on a commission of guarantors agreed by both sides to keep the talks going.
